newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee pulls back in a technical correction.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee pulls back in a technical correction.

text.p: CSCE coffee's staggering rally came to a halt on Friday, as nervous speculators moved to liquidate long positions, traders said.
After surging some 30 cents per lb -- or about 15 percent -- the last four consecutive sessions and starting today's session higher, they said the market was ripe for a correction.
"It was strictly a technical correction, " said Smith Barney analyst Walt Spilka. "The market started the day extremely overbought. It opened higher and became even more overbought."
Benchmark July coffee hit a new life-of-contract high of 225.00 cents per lb in the morning, before speculative profit-taking turned the market around.
Traders said the near completion of roaster price-fixing against May and the return of origin sales after the May Day holiday on Thursday also put pressure on the market.

Downward momentum accelerated after the July contract broke through the 200.00 level, triggering a series of sell-stops which quickly drove the benchmark contract down more than 11.00 cents to a low of 211.50 cents.

But steady buying by locals helped to trim gains and by the close July stood at 216.15 cents, down 6.75 cents per lb on the day. Spot May fell 5.20 cents, to 247.55, while the back months closed 1.90 to 5.85 lower.
Despite the losses, Smith Barney's Spilka said today's downturn was probably just a temporary set back.

"The market may deserve to go a bit lower, but overall the fundamentals have not changed," he said. "The bottom line is: the season is over for most producing countries, they've sold out almost everything and there's not a lot of coffee around."
Low consumer stocks have seen the nearby spreads become sharply backwardated, with the CSCE May/July spread jumping to 30.40 cents today from 29.85 at the close on Thursday.

After Friday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 750 bags, to 42,918 bags -- the equivalent of about 170 lots -- as of May 1. Meanwhile, open interest on the May contract was still relatively high at 1,470 lots.
However, the CSCE also reported after the closes that there were 10,477 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.
Technically, traders pegged near-term support was at the day's low of 211.50 basis July and said a breach of that level could lead to a test of the psychologically crucial $2 mark.
The day's volume was moderate,at an estimated 9,678 lots.
LIFFE coffee market in London will be closed on Monday for a bank holiday, reopening on Tuesday.
